- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) or shows recent reversal, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for potential rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects in subsequent periods; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive +1.00), model tends to overreact; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.
- If sentiment shows strong bearish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive -1.00), model tends to underreact; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Mean reversion is evident when forecast deviates >5% from 14-day moving average; bring forecast back toward average in next 3–5 periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply a “horizon decay” — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per period for periods 1–5.
